name: Request Attempt Closeout Plan
description: Make request-attempt closeout lookup keyed and bounded so background judgment cleanup cannot OOM DuckDB or block unrelated foreground API routes.

userStories.title: Add request-attempt closeout projection schema
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a compact DuckDB projection table for durable request-attempt closeout evidence so cleanup can look up closeouts by key instead of scanning token-use JSON.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `src/db/duckdbMigrations/0071_requestAttemptCloseout.sql` for `app.request_attempt_closeout`.

The table has `token_use_id`, `token_use_created_at`, `request_attempt_id`, `provider_key`, `closeout_kind`, `durable_closeout_kind`, `durable_closeout_id`, `durable_closeout_ref_json`, `closed_at`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` columns.
The primary key is `(request_attempt_id, provider_key)` and there is an index on `token_use_id`.
The schema stores `token_use_id` without a foreign key to `app.token_use`.
The schema includes non-empty checks for token-use id, request attempt id, provider key, closeout kind, and durable closeout kind.
`bun run db:mig` passes
`bun test src/db/migrateDuckdb.test.ts` passes

userStories.title: Extract durable closeout projection rows
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want manifest helpers to expose durable terminal request-attempt closeout metadata so the projection service can reuse the canonical closeout predicate.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend `getDurableTerminalRequestAttemptCloseoutProofs(...)` or add a sibling helper that uses the same durable-terminal predicate.
The helper returns normalized `providerKey`, `requestAttemptId`, `closeoutKind`, `durableCloseoutRef`, `tokenUseId`, `tokenUseCreatedAt`, and non-null `closedAt` data for projection writes.
`closedAt` is chosen from request-attempt `finishedAt`, request-attempt `updatedAt`, token-use `finished_at`, token-use `started_at`, then token-use `created_at`.
Entries missing a trimmed `providerKey` or `requestAttemptId` are skipped.
`durable_closeout_kind` falls back to `entry.closeoutKind` when `durableCloseoutRef.kind` is missing or blank.
`durable_closeout_id` is null when `durableCloseoutRef.id` is missing or blank.

userStories.title: Add request-attempt closeout projection service
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a small projection service that writes closeout rows transactionally and deterministically so writers and rebuilds share one conflict rule.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `src/server/services/requestAttemptCloseoutService.ts` with functions that accept a DuckDB runner or transaction.
The service parses request attempts with existing manifest helpers and no-ops for missing or non-terminal request attempts.
The service stores `durable_closeout_ref_json` as the source durable ref JSON, not as a replacement for raw `app.token_use.request_attempts_json`.
The service keeps one row per `(request_attempt_id, provider_key)` and prefers the earliest durable terminal evidence by `(closed_at, token_use_created_at, token_use_id)`.
Conflict updates use `CASE` assignments instead of `ON CONFLICT ... WHERE` so later incoming rows refresh `updated_at` while leaving the earlier source tuple untouched.
Service tests cover projection insert idempotency and later-conflict `updated_at` refresh without source tuple replacement.
`bun test src/server/services/requestAttemptCloseoutService.test.ts` passes
`bun run db:mig` passes

userStories.title: Add bounded closeout projection rebuild
userStories.description: As an operator, I want a bounded rebuild for existing durable token-use evidence so cleanup can cut over without a permanent token-use JSON fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a bounded rebuild maintenance script or service method for `app.request_attempt_closeout`.
The rebuild scans `app.token_use` in ordered batches by `created_at` and `id`, reading only `id`, `request_attempts_json`, `created_at`, `started_at`, and `finished_at`.
The rebuild parses request attempts in TypeScript and does not use DuckDB JSON or text predicates over `request_attempts_json`.
Maintenance mode truncates and rebuilds in batches only while token-use writers are stopped and cleanup is disabled.
Online mode captures a stable `(created_at, id)` high-water mark, writes rows up to that mark into staging, and merges staging rows into the live projection without replacing newer writer output.
The rebuild applies the same deterministic ordering and conflict rule as the projection service.
Tests cover bounded rebuild and online rebuild merge preservation of live writer rows.

userStories.title: Document shared DuckDB runtime safety
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the agent handbook to document shared DuckDB runtime constraints so future background work avoids unbounded JSON or historical-table scans.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a `### Shared DuckDB Runtime Safety` subsection under `## Database` in `AGENTS.md`.
The subsection states that foreground routes, cron jobs, queues, marts, and maintenance tasks share one constrained DuckDB runtime.
The subsection discourages unbounded scans over JSON, text, or historical tables in background jobs.
The subsection requires background work to be scoped by active rows, project, dirty token, cursor, batch limit, or explicit time window.
The subsection tells future work to persist relational keys and prefer compact lookup/projection tables for maintenance state.
The subsection treats raising `DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT` as an emergency mitigation, not the root fix.
